title: Bali Villa Pre-Opening Bookkeeping: Before the First Guest
metaTitle: Bali Villa Pre-Opening Bookkeeping: Before the First Guest
metaDescription: Opening a Bali villa? Organize furniture invoices, deposits, owner funding and unpaid commitments before the first guest, with a worked IDR example.
excerpt: A practical opening-records register for villa furniture, supplier deposits, owner funding and unpaid commitments, with an illustrative IDR cash bridge.
primaryKeyword: bali villa pre opening bookkeeping records
imageAlt: Illustrative pre-opening evidence map connecting supplier documents, payment evidence, owner funding and an opening review file
faqs: Should every pre-opening payment become an operating expense?

No. A payment is evidence of cash moving, not a conclusion about accounting or tax treatment. Keep the invoice, agreement, approval and payment evidence, then have the responsible accountant review the classification.
What if the owner paid from a personal bank account?

Record the payer, beneficiary, purpose, currency and proof of payment. Link the payment to the villa document. Keep owner funding separate from guest receipts and request advice on the correct company entry.
How should a refundable supplier deposit be tracked?

Give the deposit its own reference and link it to the supplier agreement. Record the amount paid, the expected refund or settlement, and any later credit or repayment. Keep it visible until supporting evidence explains how it was resolved.
Can the first owner report include a period with no guests?

Yes. An illustrative management report can show cash paid, unpaid commitments, owner funding and unresolved records before trading starts. Label the period clearly and agree the reporting scope with your bookkeeper.
What should change when the first Airbnb reservation arrives?

Add the reservation reference, platform earnings record and bank receipt to the same document trail. Keep booking value, deductions and the money received as separate amounts so the opening records connect to ongoing reconciliation.
contentHtml:
Bali villa pre-opening bookkeeping starts before the first guest arrives. Build a register that connects every payment and commitment to its supplier, property, approval and supporting document. Separate cash already paid from amounts still owed, refundable deposits and owner funding. The result is an opening file your accountant can review rather than a bank statement full of unexplained transfers.

This guide is for an owner preparing a villa for its first bookings, an operator taking over a newly furnished property, or a manager assembling records for a remote investor. It describes a practical evidence workflow. It does not decide whether a particular purchase is deductible, capital, a company obligation or an owner's personal cost. Those conclusions depend on the actual documents and appropriate professional review.

Start with the property, payer and reporting period

Write down the villa's working name, the entity or person named on the agreements, the person approving purchases and the accounts used to pay suppliers. Set the date range for the opening file. A furnishing project may start months before the advertised opening date; beginning the register only when bookings start leaves earlier transactions disconnected.

Give each property a stable reference. If a manager is opening two villas together, retain separate property columns even when one supplier invoice covers both. Keep the original invoice intact and attach an allocation schedule explaining the split. A convenient spreadsheet subtotal cannot replace the supplier's document or establish who legally owes the money.

Agree a reporting currency and preserve original currency amounts alongside any converted figures. Record the conversion basis for review. Do not overwrite a foreign-currency invoice with an estimated rupiah amount and discard the source. A clear original record makes later exchange differences easier to investigate.

Use one register for payments and commitments

A useful opening register needs a reference, document date, supplier, description, villa, payer, original amount, currency, payment date, amount paid, amount outstanding, document link and review status. Add the purchase order or agreement reference where there is one. Include a field for the person responsible for resolving missing evidence.

Distinguish an agreed purchase from a quotation that has not been accepted. Likewise, separate a payment request from the invoice it eventually settles. Mark provisional information as provisional. Otherwise a project budget, a supplier invoice and a bank transfer can become three apparent costs for the same furniture delivery.

Keep the raw register and an exception list together. The register says what is known; the exception list says what needs checking. Use meaningful statuses such as awaiting invoice, awaiting delivery confirmation, allocation under review and deposit unresolved. Avoid a single completed checkbox that hides which evidence was actually received.

An illustrative opening cash bridge in IDR

The following figures are fictional and demonstrate record organization only. They do not prescribe accounting entries or tax treatment. Assume one owner transferred Rp 120,000,000 into the bank account used for the project. Five documented payments then left that account. The furniture supplier has a further agreed Rp 20,000,000 balance that has not yet been paid.

Illustrative movementCash movementRecord to connect
Owner funding receivedRp 120,000,000 inTransfer evidence and funding explanation
Furniture paymentRp 50,000,000 outInvoice, delivery record and unpaid balance
Linen purchaseRp 8,000,000 outSupplier invoice and item list
Photography paymentRp 6,000,000 outAgreed scope, invoice and deliverables
Refundable supplier depositRp 10,000,000 outDeposit terms and settlement reference
Cleaning suppliesRp 4,000,000 outReceipt and property reference
Cash remaining from these movementsRp 42,000,000Bank reconciliation

Total cash paid is Rp 78,000,000. Subtracting it from Rp 120,000,000 gives Rp 42,000,000. The unpaid furniture commitment of Rp 20,000,000 does not reduce the bank balance until paid; show it separately when planning available cash. If that is the only remaining commitment, the illustrative balance after paying it would be Rp 22,000,000.

Neither Rp 78,000,000 nor Rp 98,000,000 should automatically be labelled the month's operating expense. The deposit, furniture and other items need classification review. Owner funding is also a separate question from guest revenue. Keeping these distinctions visible is the purpose of the bridge.

Build a document trail for the difficult items

Furniture and equipment: retain item descriptions, quantities, invoice references, delivery dates and the property receiving them. Where one payment covers several purchases, list the documents it settles. Where one purchase is paid in instalments, connect all payments to the same agreement so the full price is not counted repeatedly.

Deposits and advances: record who holds the money, why it was paid and how it should be settled or returned under the agreement. Add a follow-up date chosen for the project. When a final invoice arrives, attach the evidence showing how the advance was applied. Do not close an unresolved deposit simply because opening day has passed.

Owner-paid purchases: retain the owner's payment evidence and the supplier document. Record whether reimbursement has been requested, paid or left for review. A purchase paid personally must not appear as a second cash payment from the villa account when the owner later submits the receipt.

Shared purchases: document the allocation method before issuing separate owner summaries. An even split may be convenient but may not describe which villa received the goods. Keep the chosen basis, approving person and any later correction alongside the original invoice.

Three mistakes to catch before the first monthly close

Counting an advance and final invoice twice. Correct this by linking both records to one supplier agreement. The final invoice should show the full supply and the settlement trail should explain payments already made. Review the outstanding balance using documents rather than assuming that two transfers mean two separate purchases.

Treating all owner transfers as booking income. Correct this by keeping a separate funding schedule with the sender, date, amount and explanation. Money arriving in a project bank account can have several purposes. The responsible accountant needs the agreement and circumstances before deciding its treatment.

Declaring the opening file complete because the bank balances. Correct this by reviewing unpaid commitments, missing receipts and deposits as well as cleared payments. A bank reconciliation can be arithmetically correct while the underlying evidence is incomplete. Tell the owner what remains unresolved and who is following up.

A checklist for handing over the opening file

  • Confirm the villa reference, reporting period, payer accounts and responsible contacts.
  • Keep supplier invoices, agreements, receipts and payment evidence in linked folders.
  • Match each payment to its documents and identify part-payments explicitly.
  • List unpaid commitments separately from the observed bank balance.
  • Track refundable deposits and advances until their settlement is evidenced.
  • Prepare an owner-funding and reimbursement schedule.
  • Explain shared-property allocations and retain approvals.
  • List missing evidence, the next action and the person responsible.
  • Request classification review before describing the opening costs as final expenses.

Use a dated handover version so the owner and bookkeeper know which register was reviewed. If a receipt arrives afterwards, add it with a clear revision note. Preserve the earlier report rather than silently replacing an explanation that someone has already used for a funding decision.

Connect the opening file to the first bookings

Once reservations begin, add booking references and platform settlement records to the process. Airbnb's own earnings documentation describes reports and downloadable earnings data. Check the options available in the actual host account, retain the original export and record its date and filters. A dashboard total on its own does not explain every bank receipt.

Keep the opening cash bridge separate from the first trading-period report. Connect the closing project balance to the next period's opening bank balance, retain the remaining commitments and carry forward unresolved questions. This gives the first owner review a clear starting point without treating every pre-opening transfer as a guest transaction.

For the ongoing service, see monthly villa financial reporting in Bali. The journal guides on bookkeeping opening balances and PT PMA owner-funding records address related handover questions. Booking and payout records belong in a separate Airbnb and OTA reconciliation workflow.

Discuss the records before agreeing the scope

Bring a sample register, one bank statement and a short list of missing documents to the initial discussion. Explain whether the villa is owned personally or operated through a company, who holds the supplier agreements and how many properties share costs. These facts help define a useful bookkeeping scope; they do not establish a universal accounting answer.

Compare the current bookkeeping packages and inclusions, then contact Client Advisory about your opening records. You can also request a consultation on WhatsApp. Historical cleanup, specialist advice and other work require an agreed scope; a package name alone does not confirm coverage.

A review-ready exception log for opening day

Before handing over the opening register, give each unresolved item an explicit next action. A missing invoice, an undelivered purchase and an unreturned deposit are different questions. Recording them as one unexplained balance makes the next review harder. Use the same supplier and payment references as the register so the reviewer can move from the exception to the evidence without rebuilding the transaction history.

Illustrative exceptionEvidence to requestClosure condition
Furniture balance of Rp 20,000,000 remains unpaidSupplier statement and agreed delivery or payment termsRecord the reviewed balance; attach payment evidence when settled
Supplier deposit of Rp 10,000,000 remains unresolvedDeposit agreement and supplier settlement confirmationLink the refund or application against an invoice
Owner submits a receipt after the handoverOriginal invoice, payer evidence and reimbursement statusDocument review and update the funding or reimbursement schedule

These are follow-up controls for the fictional example above, not additional payments. The unpaid Rp 20,000,000 furniture balance is already part of the commitment schedule. The Rp 10,000,000 deposit is already included in the Rp 78,000,000 paid. Adding either amount to cash paid a second time would break the bridge. Keep the observed bank balance at Rp 42,000,000 until actual, evidenced movements change it.

Assign a responsible contact and a practical follow-up date to each row. Keep the question open if the requested document is still missing; a response such as “the supplier says it is fine” does not identify an invoice, delivery or settlement. When evidence arrives, retain the prior question and add the answer, date and supporting reference. This makes later corrections understandable without implying that an unresolved item has been professionally approved.

Send the exception log with the opening register and bank reconciliation, not as an unrelated message thread. For a first consultation, redact unnecessary personal or guest details and explain how the sample relates to the villa. Confirm the document-transfer process before sharing full records. The useful outcome is an agreed list of records to review and responsibilities to follow up, rather than an unsupported promise that opening costs are already final.

Frequently asked questions

Should every pre-opening payment become an operating expense?

No. A payment is evidence of cash moving, not a conclusion about accounting or tax treatment. Keep the invoice, agreement, approval and payment evidence, then have the responsible accountant review the classification.

What if the owner paid from a personal bank account?

Record the payer, beneficiary, purpose, currency and proof of payment. Link the payment to the villa document. Keep owner funding separate from guest receipts and request advice on the correct company entry.

How should a refundable supplier deposit be tracked?

Give the deposit its own reference and link it to the supplier agreement. Record the amount paid, the expected refund or settlement, and any later credit or repayment. Keep it visible until supporting evidence explains how it was resolved.

Can the first owner report include a period with no guests?

Yes. An illustrative management report can show cash paid, unpaid commitments, owner funding and unresolved records before trading starts. Label the period clearly and agree the reporting scope with your bookkeeper.

What should change when the first Airbnb reservation arrives?

Add the reservation reference, platform earnings record and bank receipt to the same document trail. Keep booking value, deductions and the money received as separate amounts so the opening records connect to ongoing reconciliation.

Sources and editorial scope

Platform reference checked 16 November 2026: Airbnb Help Centre: Download your earnings. This source supports the availability of earnings-report options, not the accounting classification of pre-opening payments. The register, checklist and IDR example are original illustrative working aids from Bali Accounting.

Illustrative process diagram created for this guide; it is not a client document.

General information only, not tax, legal or immigration advice. Actual accounting and tax treatment require case-specific professional review. Illustrative figures are not client results.

title: Bali Villa Supplier Bank Changes: A Payment Checklist
metaTitle: Bali Villa Supplier Bank Changes: A Payment Checklist
metaDescription: Check supplier bank-detail changes before paying Bali villa invoices. Use a documented approval trail, payment-hold register and worked IDR example.
excerpt: A practical supplier-change register that separates invoice approval, independent destination checks, payment release and reconciliation.
primaryKeyword: bali villa supplier bank detail change checklist
imageAlt: Illustrative supplier bank-change decision diagram: hold the payment, verify independently, approve the destination, then release and reconcile; unresolved requests stay on hold.
faqs: Should an invoice approval also approve changed bank details?
No. Keep purchase approval and payment-destination verification as separate decisions, with linked evidence and a named reviewer.
Can we verify the change by replying to the same email?
Use an independently trusted contact route instead. Record the contact source and confirmation result before changing the payee.
Does a payment hold remove the invoice from the records?
No. Retain the invoice and mark the affected payment as held. Show the unpaid amount separately from cash already transferred.
What if the owner is the only payment approver?
Document who performs each check and agree a suitable additional review step. Do not claim independent review where one person performed every role.
Does the bookkeeping package include bank-payment authority?
Confirm this in the engagement. Record preparation and reconciliation do not by themselves establish authority to change payees or release bank payments.
contentHtml:
When a Bali villa supplier asks to change bank details, pause the affected payment, verify the request through a previously trusted contact, and keep a dated approval record before updating the payee. Then connect the released payment to the original invoice and bank evidence. A familiar supplier name is not enough to explain why money went to a different account.

This guide is for villa owners, managers and bookkeepers who organize supplier payments for cleaners, laundry, maintenance and other operating purchases. It provides an original record-preparation checklist, not a bank security certification or a guarantee against fraud. Your bank's payment controls and the responsibilities agreed with your operator still apply.

Separate three questions before the payment run

First, does the invoice represent an approved purchase for the property? Second, has the proposed payment destination been checked? Third, has someone with the agreed authority approved release? These questions need different evidence. An approved repair does not automatically approve a new bank account. A verified account does not establish that the invoice is correct.

Use a stable supplier reference rather than making a new supplier whenever an account changes. Retain the earlier details in restricted history and mark their status clearly. If your system cannot retain versions, maintain a controlled change register beside it. Do not overwrite the only record of where previous payments went.

For a multi-villa operator, identify which entity owes the invoice and which bank account will pay it. A supplier may work across several properties; approval for one property's invoice should not silently authorize every pending payment. Carry the property reference through the change request, payment batch and reconciliation.

Why independent confirmation belongs in the file

NAB's business email scam guidance describes altered supplier invoices and requests to change payment details. It recommends confirming changes using an established or independently sourced telephone number rather than relying on the contact details in the incoming request. The source is Australian banking guidance, not an Indonesian legal requirement or evidence about scam frequency in Bali.

Apply that principle to the villa's existing records: use the supplier contact established before the change request, and document how it was obtained. Merely replying to the same message leaves the verification inside the channel being questioned. If the established contact cannot be reached, record the request as unresolved and keep the affected payment on hold under your agreed process.

Do not put full account details in an owner newsletter or a widely shared task board. The working payment file can retain the necessary restricted evidence while a management summary uses the supplier reference, amount and status. Agree who can edit the payee record and who can read the supporting documents.

A supplier change checklist you can adapt

StageRecord to keepQuestion before moving on
ReceiveOriginal request, date, supplier reference and affected invoicesWhat exactly is changing?
HoldPayment batch reference and hold statusCould another person release this payment?
ConfirmTrusted contact source, confirmation date and staff memberWas confirmation independent of the request?
ReviewAuthorized reviewer and decisionDoes the approved destination match the proposed payee?
ReleasePayment reference and invoice allocationIs the amount correct and still unpaid?
ReconcileBank movement and supplier settlement evidenceDoes the completed transfer match the approved instruction?

These are suggested operational fields, not mandatory legal form wording. Add the request handler, next action and follow-up date. A useful status sequence is received, awaiting independent confirmation, awaiting approval, approved for release, paid and reconciled. Preserve rejected or withdrawn requests with a short explanation rather than deleting them.

An illustrative IDR payment batch

Assume a fictional villa has Rp 30,000,000 available before a supplier payment run. Three approved invoices are waiting: laundry of Rp 4,800,000, pool maintenance of Rp 3,200,000 and a repair of Rp 7,500,000. The repair supplier requests new bank details. The operator holds that payment while checking the request; the other two invoices have no unresolved changes.

Illustrative itemAmountBatch decision
Laundry invoiceRp 4,800,000Release after normal approval
Pool maintenance invoiceRp 3,200,000Release after normal approval
Repair invoiceRp 7,500,000Hold pending destination verification
Total approved invoices awaiting payment initiallyRp 15,500,000Includes the held repair
Cash paid in the first runRp 8,000,000Laundry plus pool maintenance
Cash remaining after that runRp 22,000,000Before any other movement

The arithmetic is Rp 4,800,000 + Rp 3,200,000 = Rp 8,000,000, then Rp 30,000,000 minus Rp 8,000,000 = Rp 22,000,000. The repair remains a separate Rp 7,500,000 pending item. If independently verified, approved and subsequently paid in full, the remaining cash would be Rp 14,500,000, assuming no other movements.

The hold changes payment timing, not the invoice's underlying amount. Do not create a second repair cost when the destination is updated. The example does not prescribe revenue recognition, tax deductibility or a journal entry. It illustrates why a bank balance, a payment queue and an outstanding-invoice list need separate labels.

Keep approval and release connected

Where practical, assign the person updating the supplier details and the person approving payment separate responsibilities. Record the review in the same controlled file as the request. A second person cannot check effectively if the only information available is a screenshot saying “approved” without a supplier reference or destination version.

For a small operation where the owner performs both roles, write down that limitation and agree an additional review step suitable for the business. Do not describe a single-person workflow as independently reviewed. A process is easier to assess when the record says who actually performed each check.

Before release, compare the prepared transfer with the approved payee version and invoice balance. Recheck that the invoice was not already included in another batch. After release, attach the bank reference and settlement status. A prepared transfer, an approved transfer and a completed bank debit are different events.

Handle urgent and incomplete requests explicitly

A supplier may say that work will stop unless the payment is made immediately. Put that operational concern in the exception record and contact the authorized manager. Urgency does not supply missing verification evidence. Agree how the business will handle the disruption while preserving the unresolved status of the destination request.

If someone asks for payment to an account held under a different name, capture the explanation and request review before release. Do not infer that the arrangement is either legitimate or fraudulent from the name alone. The responsible reviewer needs the supplier relationship, supporting instruction and relevant circumstances.

If money may already have been misdirected, contact the paying bank promptly using its official contact channel and preserve the request, approval trail and transfer reference. Ask the bank about its incident procedure. Do not promise a reversal or send a replacement payment merely because the original sender says the first one failed.

Close the month without hiding the exception

At month end, list unresolved changes beside the affected invoices. Show what was paid, what remains pending and who is following up. A clean bank reconciliation does not resolve a supplier request that never reached payment. Likewise, an open request should not appear as cash already spent in an owner report.

For the fictional example, the initial owner summary can show Rp 8,000,000 paid and Rp 7,500,000 held, with Rp 22,000,000 remaining from the stated starting cash. If the repair is later released, carry its reference into the following report and reconcile the actual date. Preserve the earlier report so readers understand the sequence.

At handover, review which staff can edit supplier details, release payments and access the change register. Remove obsolete access through your existing account-management process. Transfer the unresolved list as well as the approved supplier file, so a new manager does not mistake an old payment hold for a routine unpaid bill.

Connect this control to the bookkeeping service

Our villa payroll and supplier-records service is the existing commercial home for organizing these records. Ask which document checks, payment responsibilities and reporting deliverables are included in your engagement. Do not assume that bookkeeping automatically authorizes a provider to operate your bank account or certify a payee.

For related controls, read duplicate invoices and credit notes and the supplier invoice and payroll control workflow. Those guides address invoice identity and routine collection; this checklist addresses a change in payment destination.

Compare current bookkeeping packages and inclusions, then contact Client Advisory with a redacted sample of your supplier register. You can also request a consultation on WhatsApp. Agree a secure document-transfer method before sharing full banking records. No additional service price or bank authority is implied by this guide.

Frequently asked questions

Should an invoice approval also approve changed bank details?

No. Keep purchase approval and payment-destination verification as separate decisions, with linked evidence and a named reviewer.

Can we verify the change by replying to the same email?

Use an independently trusted contact route instead. Record the contact source and confirmation result before changing the payee.

Does a payment hold remove the invoice from the records?

No. Retain the invoice and mark the affected payment as held. Show the unpaid amount separately from cash already transferred.

What if the owner is the only payment approver?

Document who performs each check and agree a suitable additional review step. Do not claim independent review where one person performed every role.

Does the bookkeeping package include bank-payment authority?

Confirm this in the engagement. Record preparation and reconciliation do not by themselves establish authority to change payees or release bank payments.

Source and scope

Primary banking guidance accessed 19 November 2026: NAB: Protect your business from email scams. It supports independent confirmation of changed payment details and consideration of separated payment duties. Australian bank products and reporting numbers are not presented as Indonesian services. The checklist, villa scenario and diagram are original illustrative working aids, not client records. General information only, not tax, legal or immigration advice, a fraud investigation, or a guarantee of payment security.

title: Airbnb Co-Host Payouts: Reconcile the Owner's Share
metaDescription: Reconcile Airbnb co-host payouts for a Bali villa with a booking-level cash bridge, separate receipt checks and an illustrative IDR example.
excerpt: Connect one booking to the owner's and co-host's separate payouts. Build a clear cash bridge, confirm receipts and avoid paying the same obligation twice.
imageAlt: Illustrative IDR cash bridge: 10.5 million less 0.5 million equals 10 million, allocated 8 million to the owner and 2 million to the co-host, with separate receipt evidence.
contentHtml:
Reconcile the booking before checking each recipient

When Airbnb pays part of a booking to a co-host, reconcile the booking to both allocations, then match each allocation to its own receipt evidence. The owner's bank deposit alone cannot explain the full settlement. Keep the reservation reference, platform deductions, agreed split, payout references and unresolved amounts together. This is a practical approach to Airbnb co-host payout reconciliation for a Bali villa's records, rather than a method for deciding who legally earns the booking income.

Who this applies to

This guide is for Bali villa owners and managers preparing records where an Airbnb home reservation has a co-host payout. It is particularly useful when an overseas owner receives one amount and a local operator receives another. It also helps the person preparing an owner statement explain a smaller bank receipt without describing the difference as missing money.

Check the account and listing actually involved. Airbnb identifies location-based restrictions in its regional limitations for co-host payouts. This guide does not establish that a particular arrangement is eligible. It also does not cover setting up payouts or selecting an Indonesian tax treatment.

For help connecting platform activity to monthly records, see our Airbnb bookkeeping service in Bali. See also Bali Accounting's villa bookkeeping and reporting overview. An engagement should identify which entity's books are being prepared, which records the client can provide and which questions require separate advice.

Separate the payout instruction from the accounting conclusion

Airbnb's co-host payout guidance describes cleaning-fee, percentage and fixed-amount options. A payout instruction describes the movement of money; your bookkeeping file still needs the underlying agreement and supporting records. Do not infer ownership of income, an expense classification or an outstanding invoice solely from the recipient's name.

Use three separate questions. What did the platform allocate? What did each recipient actually receive? What does the agreement say the payment settles? The first two support a cash reconciliation. The third helps the responsible accountant assess the appropriate records and treatment. Keeping these questions separate prevents an apparently neat spreadsheet from concealing an unsupported assumption.

Also distinguish a co-host payment from routing money between payout methods. Airbnb documents those instructions separately in its split-payout guidance. Name the actual arrangement in the reconciliation register rather than using “split” as a catch-all description. A destination bank account is not, by itself, an explanation of the commercial relationship.

Build one booking-level evidence register

Start with one reservation reference and connect every settlement component to it. Record the property, operating entity, stay dates, reporting period, currency, platform amount, deductions, co-host allocation and owner allocation. Give each payout its own reference and status. Attach the original report rather than repeatedly replacing a spreadsheet total with the latest number.

The register should distinguish an expected allocation from a confirmed receipt. Use simple statuses such as allocated, released, receipt confirmed and unresolved. These are suggested internal labels, not Airbnb interface labels. Keep the person responsible for resolving each open item visible, together with the question they need to answer.

Collect only the evidence needed for that question. A recipient may provide a redacted transaction confirmation showing the relevant reference, date, currency and amount. Avoid requesting unrelated personal transactions. If evidence cannot be shared yet, retain the item as unconfirmed and state exactly what remains missing.

Airbnb says listing owners cannot access a co-host's transaction history. Its explanation of co-host earnings visibility is an important reason to agree an evidence handover in advance. Seeing an allocation in the host's account is not the same as independently confirming its arrival in another person's bank.

An illustrative IDR settlement bridge

The following figures are entirely illustrative. Assume one reservation's platform report shows IDR 10,500,000 before a separately identified deduction of IDR 500,000. The remaining settlement is IDR 10,000,000. For this example only, the confirmed allocation assigns a fixed IDR 2,000,000 to the co-host and IDR 8,000,000 to the owner. These are invented amounts, not published platform charges, standard management fees or client results.

Illustrative cash allocation for reservation EX-1101
ComponentIllustrative IDR amountEvidence to connect
Reported amount before the example deduction10,500,000Reservation and platform breakdown
Separately documented deduction500,000Platform deduction line and supporting record
Amount available for the illustrated allocation10,000,00010,500,000 minus 500,000
Owner allocation8,000,000Allocation instruction and owner payout reference
Co-host allocation2,000,000Allocation instruction and co-host payout reference
Total allocated10,000,0008,000,000 plus 2,000,000

The owner's IDR 8,000,000 bank receipt is IDR 2,000,000 lower than the amount available for allocation. That difference is explained by the co-host allocation, provided the supporting records agree. It is not automatically another platform fee, an unpaid guest balance or a second expense. Record the deduction once and each allocation once.

This table is a selected cash bridge. It is not a complete journal entry, trial balance, profit calculation or tax calculation. The appropriate revenue presentation and treatment of the co-host payment depend on the agreement, entity and accounting assessment. A correct addition does not settle those separate questions.

Explain receipts that fall into different months

Now assume the example allocation is visible on 31 October, the owner confirms receipt on 2 November and the co-host confirms receipt on 4 November. These dates illustrate a record trail, not expected processing times or a payment promise.

At the October checkpoint, IDR 10,000,000 remains unconfirmed as received in this illustrative schedule. After the owner's confirmation, IDR 8,000,000 is matched and IDR 2,000,000 remains unconfirmed. After both confirmations, the unconfirmed amount is zero. Preserve the platform release dates separately from these receipt dates.

Do not change the stay dates to make the cash schedule balance. Keep the reservation period, platform activity date and bank receipt date in separate fields. Let the accountant decide the appropriate reporting treatment. The schedule's job is to explain the evidence and timing, including any amount whose destination is still unconfirmed.

For a wider reporting view, our guide to what belongs in a villa owner statement explains how cash movements and open items can sit alongside operating results.

A decision aid for differences

  • The allocation totals agree, but a bank receipt is missing: retain the payout reference and ask for receipt confirmation. Do not invent a receipt date.
  • The two allocations do not add to the reported settlement: inspect the selected reservation, currency, deductions and applicable instruction before changing the records.
  • The cash matches, but an invoice also appears unpaid: establish whether the platform payment settles that invoice or a different obligation. Link the documents before considering another transfer.
  • A later adjustment appears: link it to the original booking and actual adjustment record. Do not automatically apply the original split to a refund or infer the platform's recovery method.
  • The parties disagree about what the allocation covers: mark the commercial question unresolved and refer to the agreement. Keep the confirmed cash trail intact.

What owners get wrong

Counting only the owner's receipt. This leaves the other allocation unexplained. Correct it by building the booking-level bridge first, then matching the separate destinations. Do not turn the unexplained difference into a balancing expense.

Paying the same obligation again. A co-host may send an invoice while the platform has already transferred an amount connected to that work. Correct it by documenting what each payment settles. An invoice number, reservation reference and recipient confirmation are more useful than assuming all similar amounts are duplicates.

Combining different parties' income in one report. A cash register covering the booking can help explain settlement, but it is not permission to combine the owner's and manager's accounts. Correct it by identifying the reporting entity and keeping the allocation schedule distinct from its financial statements.

Our guide to owner liabilities and management-company revenue provides related context for keeping those records separate.

A month-end handover checklist

  1. Identify the reservation, villa, reporting entity, currency and period.
  2. Save the original platform breakdown and applicable allocation instruction.
  3. Connect each deduction and allocation without counting any component twice.
  4. Match each available payout reference to relevant receipt evidence.
  5. List unconfirmed receipts and commercial questions with an owner and next action.
  6. Link invoices, adjustments and later confirmations to the same reservation record.
  7. Check the report includes the intended listings and date range.
  8. Retain the completed version and the original supporting files.

Airbnb's earnings-download guidance describes reports and exports with filters and earnings details. Use the options actually available in the relevant account, and record the report period. Avoid hard-coding a menu sequence into your internal process because interfaces and available options may differ.

A useful handover note explains the remaining exception precisely: “Co-host allocation recorded; receipt evidence requested; no additional payment approved.” This lets the next person continue the work without confusing missing documentation with missing cash.

Before closing the file, ask someone to follow one reservation from the original report to the register and then to the available receipt evidence. They should be able to identify which figures are confirmed, which are expected and which question remains open without relying on a verbal explanation. Keep the report filters and export date alongside the file so a later reviewer can reproduce that check.

Agree the records before the next close

Decide who obtains the host report, who confirms the co-host receipt and who reviews unresolved items. Keep commercial interpretation with the appropriately responsible person. A bookkeeper should not have to reconstruct an agreement from bank descriptions after each stay.

Frequently asked questions

Is the owner's bank receipt the full booking amount?

Not necessarily. For the illustrated arrangement, it is one part of the settlement after the stated deduction and co-host allocation. Reconcile the complete booking breakdown before interpreting an individual deposit.

Can the owner see the co-host's transaction history?

Airbnb says listing owners cannot access that history. Agree an appropriate confirmation process with the co-host and distinguish the visible allocation from evidence that the recipient actually received it.

Does a co-host allocation automatically settle a management invoice?

No conclusion should be drawn from the amount alone. Check the agreement, invoice and reservation reference, then document whether the transfer settles that obligation. Hold a further payment decision until the connection is clear.

What if the two receipts arrive in different months?

Keep their actual receipt dates and the original booking reference. Show any unconfirmed balance in the cash schedule and let the accountant assess the appropriate reporting treatment separately.

Does this establish the correct Indonesian tax treatment?

No. The register explains settlement evidence. It does not decide taxable income, deductibility or filing obligations. Those questions require the actual facts and appropriately qualified advice.
